intended_object: The reduction homomorphism W(K) → W(F) for an elliptic curve W over F, base-changed to an extension K, at a place w of K/F whose residue field is F (degree one). In the sense of Silverman VII.2.1, integral points go to the residues of their coordinates, and points where x has a pole go to O. Inferred from the docstring and the module documentation.
explanation:
The map sends A to a point Q of W(F) with A − Q in `polePoints W w`. That subgroup is {O} together with the points whose x-coordinate has a pole at w, i.e. the kernel of reduction E₁. The file proves that Q exists (`exists_sub_mem_polePoints`, which uses that w has degree one) and that it is unique (`eq_of_sub_mem_polePoints`), so the choice made with `.choose` is fully determined.

This gives exactly the classical reduction map:
- If (x, y) is integral with x ≡ a and y ≡ b mod w, it goes to (a, b) (`reductionOfDegreeEqOne_some`).
- Points where x has a pole, and O, go to O.
- The kernel is E₁ (`ker_reductionOfDegreeEqOne`).
- Points of W(F) are fixed (`reductionOfDegreeEqOne_baseChange`).

Additivity follows because E₁ is a subgroup, which matches the standard argument.

The special setting is needed by the definition itself. A curve defined over the constant field F, together with a place of degree one, is what makes the target W(F) rather than W over some abstract residue field. The general version, reduction into the projective plane over the residue field at an arbitrary valuation, exists separately in the library (`WeierstrassCurve.Affine.Point.reduction`). Mathlib has no reduction map for elliptic-curve points, so there is no broader Mathlib counterpart.
